study type: Secondary analysis of population survey data
exposure: Women who had a vaginal birth
Women's perceived ability to 'take their time' in labor
outcome: Determinants of having a vaginal birth
Determinants of having a normal birth
cohort: 772 women who gave birth in Queensland, Australia during a two-week period in 2009
finding: Women who birthed in public hospitals, birthed outside of regular business hours, had mobility in labor, did not have continuous fetal monitoring, and were non-supine during birth had significantly higher odds of experiencing a normal birth.
mod_finding: Women who had a vaginal birth had significantly higher odds of having a normal birth if they birthed in a public hospital, birthed outside regular business hours, had mobility in labor, did not have continuous fetal monitoring, and were non-supine during birth.
